# Skill: frontend-ui-engineering # Frontend UI Engineering ## Overview Build production-quality user interfaces that are accessible, performant, and visually polished. The goal is UI that looks like it was built by a design-aware engineer at a top company — not like it was generated by an AI. This means real design system adherence, proper accessibility, thoughtful interaction patterns, and no generic "AI aesthetic." ## When to Use - Building new UI components or pages - Modifying existing user-facing interfaces - Implementing responsive layouts - Adding interactivity or state management - Fixing visual or UX issues ## Component Architecture ### File Structure Colocate everything related to a component: ``` src/components/ TaskList/ TaskList.tsx # Component implementation TaskList.test.tsx # Tests TaskList.stories.tsx # Storybook stories (if using) use-task-list.ts # Custom hook (if complex state) types.ts # Component-specific types (if needed) ``` ### Component Patterns **Prefer composition over configuration:** ```tsx // Good: Composable Tasks // Avoid: Over-configured } /> ``` **Keep components focused:** ```tsx // Good: Does one thing export function TaskItem({ task, onToggle, onDelete }: TaskItemProps) { return (
  • onToggle(task.id)} /> {task.title}
    • ); } ``` **Separate data fetching from presentation:** ```tsx // Container: handles data export function TaskListContainer() { const { tasks, isLoading, error, refetch } = useTasks(); if (isLoading) return ; if (error) return ; if (tasks.length === 0) return ; return ; } // Presentation: handles rendering export function TaskList({ tasks }: { tasks: Task[] }) { return (
      {tasks.map(task => )}
    ); } ``` ## State Management **Choose the simplest approach that works:** ``` Local state (useState) → Component-specific UI state Lifted state → Shared between 2-3 sibling components Context → Theme, auth, locale (read-heavy, write-rare) URL state (searchParams) → Filters, pagination, shareable UI state Server state (React Query, SWR) → Remote data with caching Global store (Zustand, Redux) → Complex client state shared app-wide ``` **Avoid prop drilling deeper than 3 levels.** If you're passing props through components that don't use them, introduce context or restructure the component tree. ## Design System Adherence ### Reference-led UI quality When the product needs a distinct visual direction, collect evidence before choosing a layout: 1. Search a trusted reference catalogue or use references supplied by the product team. 2. Study two or three relevant screens. Record decisions about hierarchy, density, navigation, controls, responsive behavior, and interaction states. 3. Turn those decisions into a short design contract before implementation. Name the screen's job, primary action, required states, responsive rules, and patterns to reject. 4. Rebuild the useful structure in the product's own components, tokens, content, and visual language. Never copy another product's branding, proprietary text, imagery, or exact layout. Use references as evidence, not as templates. If references are unavailable, document the assumptions and verify the result against the product's existing design system. ### Avoid the AI Aesthetic AI-generated UI has recognizable patterns. Avoid all of them: | AI Default | Why It Is a Problem | Production Quality | |---|---|---| | Purple/indigo everything | Models default to visually "safe" palettes, making every app look identical | Use the project's actual color palette | | Excessive gradients | Gradients add visual noise and clash with most design systems | Flat or subtle gradients matching the design system | | Rounded everything (rounded-2xl) | Maximum rounding signals "friendly" but ignores the hierarchy of corner radii in real designs | Consistent border-radius from the design system | | Generic hero sections | Template-driven layout with no connection to the actual content or user need | Content-first layouts | | Lorem ipsum-style copy | Placeholder text hides layout problems that real content reveals (length, wrapping, overflow) | Realistic placeholder content | | Oversized padding everywhere | Equal generous padding destroys visual hierarchy and wastes screen space | Consistent spacing scale | | Stock card grids | Uniform grids are a layout shortcut that ignores information priority and scanning patterns | Purpose-driven layouts | | Shadow-heavy design | Layered shadows add depth that competes with content and slows rendering on low-end devices | Subtle or no shadows unless the design system specifies | ### Spacing and Layout Use a consistent spacing scale. Don't invent values: ```css /* Use the scale: 0.25rem increments (or whatever the project uses) */ /* Good */ padding: 1rem; /* 16px */ /* Good */ gap: 0.75rem; /* 12px */ /* Bad */ padding: 13px; /* Not on any scale */ /* Bad */ margin-top: 2.3rem; /* Not on any scale */ ``` ### Typography Respect the type hierarchy: ``` h1 → Page title (one per page) h2 → Section title h3 → Subsection title body → Default text small → Secondary/helper text ``` Don't skip heading levels. Don't use heading styles for non-heading content. ### Color - Use semantic color tokens: `text-primary`, `bg-surface`, `border-default` — not raw hex values - Ensure sufficient contrast (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text) - Don't rely solely on color to convey information (use icons, text, or patterns too) ## Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA) Every component must meet these standards: ### Keyboard Navigation ```tsx // Every interactive element must be keyboard accessible // ✓ Focusable by default
    Click me
    // ✗ Not focusable
    onKeyDown={e => { if (e.key === 'Enter') handleClick(); if (e.key === ' ') e.preventDefault(); }} onKeyUp={e => { if (e.key === ' ') handleClick(); }}> Click me
    ``` ### ARIA Labels ```tsx // Label interactive elements that lack visible text // Label form inputs // Or use aria-label when no visible label exists ``` ### Focus Management ```tsx // Move focus when content changes function Dialog({ isOpen, onClose }: DialogProps) { const closeRef = useRef(null); useEffect(() => { if (isOpen) closeRef.current?.focus(); }, [isOpen]); // Trap focus inside dialog when open return ( {/* dialog content */} ); } ``` ### Meaningful Empty and Error States ```tsx // Don't show blank screens function TaskList({ tasks }: { tasks: Task[] }) { if (tasks.length === 0) { return (

    No tasks

    Get started by creating a new task.

    ); } return
      ...
    ; } ``` ## Responsive Design Design for mobile first, then expand: ```tsx // Tailwind: mobile-first responsive
    ``` Test at these breakpoints: 320px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px. ## Loading and Transitions ```tsx // Skeleton loading (not spinners for content) function TaskListSkeleton() { return (
    {Array.from({ length: 3 }).map((_, i) => (
    ))}
    ); } // Optimistic updates for perceived speed function useToggleTask() { const queryClient = useQueryClient(); return useMutation({ mutationFn: toggleTask, onMutate: async (taskId) => { await queryClient.cancelQueries({ queryKey: ['tasks'] }); const previous = queryClient.getQueryData(['tasks']); queryClient.setQueryData(['tasks'], (old: Task[]) => old.map(t => t.id === taskId ? { ...t, done: !t.done } : t) ); return { previous }; }, onError: (_err, _taskId, context) => { queryClient.setQueryData(['tasks'], context?.previous); }, }); } ``` ## See Also For detailed accessibility requirements and testing tools, see `../../references/accessibility-checklist.md`. ## Common Rationalizations | Rationalization | Reality | |---|---| | "Accessibility is a nice-to-have" | It's a legal requirement in many jurisdictions and an engineering quality standard. | | "We'll make it responsive later" | Retrofitting responsive design is 3x harder than building it from the start. | | "The design isn't final, so I'll skip styling" | Use the design system defaults. Unstyled UI creates a broken first impression for reviewers. | | "This is just a prototype" | Prototypes become production code. Build the foundation right. | | "The AI aesthetic is fine for now" | It signals low quality. Use the project's actual design system from the start. | ## Red Flags - Components with more than 200 lines (split them) - Inline styles or arbitrary pixel values - Missing error states, loading states, or empty states - No keyboard navigation testing - Color as the sole indicator of state (red/green without text or icons) - Generic "AI look" (purple gradients, oversized cards, stock layouts) ## Verification After building UI: - [ ] Component renders without console errors - [ ] All interactive elements are keyboard accessible (Tab through the page) - [ ] Screen reader can convey the page's content and structure - [ ] Responsive: works at 320px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px - [ ] Loading, empty, error, success, and permission states handled when applicable - [ ] Follows the project's design system (spacing, colors, typography) - [ ] The rendered result passes a final UI-specific finish-gate review - [ ] No accessibility warnings in dev tools or axe-core Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\Administrator\.agents\skills\frontend-ui-engineering Relative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory. 6. db init: `app.getPath('userData')` at module load before app ready — in main process, app is ready-ish? db.ts imports and computes dbPath at module top-level; initDb called in whenReady, fine since getPath top-level is called at import time (before ready). app.getPath('userData') before ready can throw if not set correctly... In Electron, userData path can be retrieved before ready usually fine. But better move into initDb.
7. db persist interval of 2000 ms writes entire DB — heavy; also setInterval keeps process; use better scheduling (write after each mutation debounced) and close on quit. Also missing WAL etc. sql.js fine.

11. Tray icon missing: app has `skipTaskbar: true` and no tray; if you close the window the app quits (window-all-closed). For a desktop assistant, a Tray with global shortcut (toggle chat) is important. Add Tray + global shortcut (e.g., Alt+Space) for summon/dismiss, and keep app running.

## Qué encontré y qué arreglé

### Bugs funcionales (críticos)
1. **URL y modelo guardados pero ignorados** — El cliente LLM solo leía `.env`; al cambiar URL/modelo en ⚙ no se aplicaba nunca. Ahora todo se resuelve desde la BD → env → default en un solo lugar (`resolveOmniConfig`) y se aplica al vuelo.
2. **"Conectado" era fake** — Se marcaba ONLINE solo si existía una API key, sin probar nada. Ahora `openclaw:connect` y `retry` hacen una **verificación real** contra el gateway (petición mínima) y reportan el error exacto si falla.
3. **Adjuntos ignorados** — Se enviaban al chat pero el modelo nunca los veía. Ahora: **imágenes van como contenido multimodal** (image_url, para modelos con visión) y **archivos de texto** (txt/md/json/csv/log/xml…) se inyectan como texto en el prompt.
4. **Fallo de seguridad** — `files:read` te dejaba leer **cualquier archivo del disco**. Ahora valida contra las carpetas autorizadas de la pestaña DATOS.
5. **Dictado por voz se colgaba** — El callback de reinicio usaba un closure vencido de `isRecording`. Arreglado con refs; además ahora muestra correctamente si el equipo soporta dictado.

### Funciones nuevas (asistente completo y operativo)
- **Streaming en tiempo real**: las respuestas aparecen token a token con cursor animado (`openclaw:delta`), no más esperar 30s en blanco.
- **Historial persistente**: la conversación sobrevive reinicios (tabla `chat_history` existente que estaba sin usar), con botón 🗑 para limpiar en el header.
- **Bandeja del sistema (Tray)** con ícono cian generado: mostrar/ocultar y Salir. El asistente **vive en segundo plano** — cerrar la ventana no apaga la app, y hay **instancia única** (no se abren dos copias).
- **Atajo global `Ctrl+Alt+J`**: invoca/oculta al asistente desde cualquier lugar de Windows.
- **Personalidad editable**: campo de system prompt ("Personalidad") en la pestaña SISTEMA, sincronizado sin reiniciar.
- **Botón copiar** en cada respuesta del asistente, **Esc cierra** el chat, composer con **textarea multilínea** auto-creciente (Shift+Enter = nueva línea), timestamps reales por mensaje.

### Limpieza

function Save-Cropped([System.Drawing.Bitmap]$bitmap, [int]$cx, [int]$cy, [int]$cw, [int]$ch, [string]$outPath, [int]$outSize) {
    # Cuadrado del side del contenido más ancho; el contenido se CENTRA verticalmente,
    # de modo que nunca se arrastran filas ajenas ( ej. el wordmark que está debajo).
    $square = [Math]::Max($cw, $ch)
    $out = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap($outSize, $outSize)
    $g = [System.Drawing.Graphics]::FromImage($out)
    $g.InterpolationMode = [System.Drawing.Drawing2D.InterpolationMode]::HighQualityBicubic
    $g.SmoothingMode = 'AntiAlias'
    $g.PixelOffsetMode = [System.Drawing.Drawing2D.PixelOffsetMode]::HighQuality
    $dstY = [Math]::Floor(($square - $ch) / 2)
    $dstX = [Math]::Floor(($square - $cw) / 2)
    $g.DrawImage($bitmap,
        (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle($dstX, $dstY, $cw, $ch)),
        (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle($cx, $cy, $cw, $ch)),
        [System.Drawing.GraphicsUnit]::Pixel)
    $g.Dispose()
    $out.Save($outPath, [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png)
    $out.Dispose()
}

function Save-Cropped([System.Drawing.Bitmap]$bitmap, [int]$cx, [int]$cy, [int]$cw, [int]$ch, [string]$outPath, [int]$outSize) {
    $square = [Math]::Max($cw, $ch)
    $pad = [int]($square * 0.08)

    $g = [System.Drawing.Graphics]::FromImage($out)
    $g.InterpolationMode = [System.Drawing.Drawing2D.InterpolationMode]::HighQualityBicubic
    $g.SmoothingMode = 'AntiAlias'
    $g.PixelOffsetMode = [System.Drawing.Drawing2D.PixelOffsetMode]::HighQuality
    $g.DrawImage($bitmap, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(0, 0, $outSize, $outSize)), $sq, [System.Drawing.GraphicsUnit]::Pixel)
    $g.Dispose()
    $out.Save($outPath, [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png)
    $out.Dispose()
}

input.content:
# IA-companion-GS

Asistente de escritorio con IA (Electron + React) para Windows: burbuja flotante siempre visible, chat con streaming, voz (TTS), dictado por voz, adjuntos multimodales y **compatibilidad con cualquier proveedor de modelos** (no depende de un único gateway).

![IA-companion-GS](src/renderer/assets/logo.png)

## Características

- 💬 **Chat con streaming** — las respuestas aparecen en tiempo real (SSE compatible OpenAI).
- 🌐 **Cualquier proveedor** — presets listos: OmniRoute/OpenClaw local, OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, DeepSeek, Gemini, Ollama y LM Studio. También endpoints personalizados.
- 🖼️ **Adjuntos multimodales** — imágenes (modelos con visión) y archivos de texto (txt/md/json/csv/log…) se envían al modelo.
- 🔊 **TTS multi-proveedor** — Fish Audio, OpenAI TTS y ElevenLabs, con auto-voz opcional.
- 🎙️ **Dictado por voz** — reconocimiento de voz integrado (es-AR, continua).
- 🧲 **Burbuja flotante + bandeja del sistema** — vive en segundo plano; cierre de ventana ≠ cierre de la app.
- ⌨️ **Atajo global** — `Ctrl+Alt+J` invoca / oculta el asistente desde cualquier parte.
- 🗂️ **Historial persistente** — la conversación sobrevive reinicios (SQLite); botón para limpiar.
- 🔒 **Permisos de carpetas** — la lectura de archivos solo se permite en carpetas que autorizás explícitamente.
- 🧠 **Personalidad editable** — prompt de sistema configurable desde Ajustes.

## Requisitos

- **Node.js ≥ 20** (LTS recomendado)
- **npm** (o pnpm)
- Una API key de alguno de los proveedores compatibles (o un gateway/modelo local)

## Instalación

```bash
# 1. Abrí la carpeta del proyecto
cd ia-companion-gs

# 2. Instalá dependencias
npm install

# 3. Configurá (opcional en desarrollo: todo se puede configurar desde la UI)
cp .env.example .env
# Edita .env con tus claves

# 4. Desarrollo (hot-reload)
npm run dev

# 5. Build de producción
npm run build
npm start   # ejecuta el build de dist/
```

## Proveedores de modelo

El asistente habla con **cualquier endpoint compatible con la API de chat de OpenAI**. En *Ajustes › Sistema › Proveedor de modelo* elegís el preset y completa URL + API key + modelo:

| Proveedor | URL | Ejemplo de modelo |
|-----------|-----|-------------------|
| OmniRoute (local) | `http://localhost:20128/v1` | `omniroute/default` |
| OpenRouter | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | `openai/gpt-4o-mini` |
| OpenAI | `https://api.openai.com/v1` | `gpt-4o-mini` |
| Anthropic | `https://api.anthropic.com/v1` | `claude-sonnet-4-5` |
| Groq | `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1` | `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` |
| DeepSeek | `https://api.deepseek.com/v1` | `deepseek-chat` |
| Gemini | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai` | `gemini-2.0-flash` |
| Ollama (local) | `http://localhost:11434/v1` | `llama3.2` |
| LM Studio (local) | `http://localhost:1234/v1` | nombre del modelo cargado |
| Personalizado | tu URL | tu modelo |

El botón **CONECTAR** hace una verificación real: si la URL, la key o el modelo no son válidos, te muestra el error exacto del proveedor.

También podés configurar por `.env` (se usan como valores por defecto):

```bash
LLM_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1   # o OMNIROUTE_URL (compatibilidad)
LLM_API_KEY=sk-...                      # o OMNIROUTE_API_KEY
LLM_MODEL=vendor/modelo                 # o OMNIROUTE_MODEL
```

## Variables de entorno (`.env`)

| Variable | Descripción |
|----------|-------------|
| `LLM_URL` / `OMNIROUTE_URL` | URL del proveedor (compat. OpenAI). |
| `LLM_API_KEY` / `OMNIROUTE_API_KEY` | API key del proveedor. |
| `LLM_MODEL` / `OMNIROUTE_MODEL` | Modelo a usar. |
| `FISH_API_KEY` | API key de Fish Audio (TTS). |
| `FISH_REFERENCE_ID` | ID de voz clonada en Fish Audio (opcional). |
| `FISH_MODEL` | Modelo de Fish Audio (default `s2.1-pro-free`). |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | API key de OpenAI (TTS). |
| `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` | API key de ElevenLabs (TTS). |

Todo esto también se configura desde la ventana de Ajustes (⚙) y se guarda en SQLite local.

## Scripts disponibles

| Script | Qué hace |
|--------|----------|
| `npm run dev` | Electron + Vite en modo desarrollo (hot-reload). |
| `npm run build` | Compila main, preload y renderer a `dist/`. |
| `npm start` | Ejecuta el build de producción (`electron .`). |
| `npm run preview` | Previsualización del build. |
| `npm run type-check` | `tsc --noEmit`. |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint. |
| `npm run test` | Vitest. |

## Uso

- **Burbuja**: clic sobre la burbuja flotante (abajo a la derecha) abre el chat.
- **Atajo**: `Ctrl+Alt+J` muestra/oculta el asistente.
- **Bandeja**: ícono en la bandeja del sistema con "Mostrar / ocultar" y "Salir".
- **Escape**: cierra el panel del chat (la app sigue en la bandeja).
- **Adjuntar**: 📎 en el composer; las imágenes van al modelo como visión, los textos se inyectan al prompt.
- **Dictado**: botón ♪ (requiere soporte de reconocimiento de voz en el sistema).
- **Ajustes (⚙)**: proveedor de modelo, personalidad, TTS, carpetas autorizadas.

## Estructura del proyecto

```
ia-companion-gs/
├── build/                      # Logo e íconos (icon.png / icon.ico / ia-logo-full.png)
├── src/
│   ├── main/                   # Proceso principal (Electron)
│   │   ├── index.ts            # Entry point, instancia única, tray, atajo global
│   │   ├── window-manager.ts   # Ventana burbuja flotante
│   │   ├── model-client.ts     # Cliente LLM (OpenAI-compatible, streaming SSE)
│   │   ├── tts-providers.ts    # Registry TTS (Fish/OpenAI/ElevenLabs)
│   │   ├── ipc-handlers.ts     # Puente main ↔ renderer, chat, historial, archivos
│   │   ├── file-permissions.ts # Autorización de carpetas
│   │   ├── db.ts               # SQLite (sql.js) ajustes + historial
│   │   └── tray.ts             # Bandeja del sistema
│   ├── preload/
│   │   └── index.ts            # contextBridge seguro
│   └── renderer/               # UI React + Vite
│       ├── assets/             # Logo (logo.png / icon-mark.png)
│       ├── bubble/             # Burbuja flotante clickeable
│       ├── chat/               # Ventana de chat
│       ├── image-viewer/       # Visor de adjuntos
│       └── settings/           # Ajustes (proveedor, voz, datos, info)
└── docs/
```

## Seguridad

- `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false` y preload mínimo vía `contextBridge`.
- **CSP** configurada en el renderer.
- La API key y los ajustes se guardan en SQLite en `%APPDATA%/ia-companion-gs/` (no en el repo).
- La lectura de archivos del disco exige carpetas autorizadas por el usuario.
- Instancia única (`requestSingleInstanceLock`): no se abren dos copias.

## Licencia

MIT — Úsalo, modifícalo y compártelo libremente.

# Skill: frontend-ui-engineering # Frontend UI Engineering ## Overview Build production-quality user interfaces that are accessible, performant, and visually polished. The goal is UI that looks like it was built by a design-aware engineer at a top company — not like it was generated by an AI. This means real design system adherence, proper accessibility, thoughtful interaction patterns, and no generic "AI aesthetic." ## When to Use - Building new UI components or pages - Modifying existing user-facing interfaces - Implementing responsive layouts - Adding interactivity or state management - Fixing visual or UX issues ## Component Architecture ### File Structure Colocate everything related to a component: ``` src/components/ TaskList/ TaskList.tsx # Component implementation TaskList.test.tsx # Tests TaskList.stories.tsx # Storybook stories (if using) use-task-list.ts # Custom hook (if complex state) types.ts # Component-specific types (if needed) ``` ### Component Patterns **Prefer composition over configuration:** ```tsx // Good: Composable Tasks // Avoid: Over-configured } /> ``` **Keep components focused:** ```tsx // Good: Does one thing export function TaskItem({ task, onToggle, onDelete }: TaskItemProps) { return (
  • onToggle(task.id)} /> {task.title}
    • ); } ``` **Separate data fetching from presentation:** ```tsx // Container: handles data export function TaskListContainer() { const { tasks, isLoading, error, refetch } = useTasks(); if (isLoading) return ; if (error) return ; if (tasks.length === 0) return ; return ; } // Presentation: handles rendering export function TaskList({ tasks }: { tasks: Task[] }) { return (
      {tasks.map(task => )}
    ); } ``` ## State Management **Choose the simplest approach that works:** ``` Local state (useState) → Component-specific UI state Lifted state → Shared between 2-3 sibling components Context → Theme, auth, locale (read-heavy, write-rare) URL state (searchParams) → Filters, pagination, shareable UI state Server state (React Query, SWR) → Remote data with caching Global store (Zustand, Redux) → Complex client state shared app-wide ``` **Avoid prop drilling deeper than 3 levels.** If you're passing props through components that don't use them, introduce context or restructure the component tree. ## Design System Adherence ### Reference-led UI quality When the product needs a distinct visual direction, collect evidence before choosing a layout: 1. Search a trusted reference catalogue or use references supplied by the product team. 2. Study two or three relevant screens. Record decisions about hierarchy, density, navigation, controls, responsive behavior, and interaction states. 3. Turn those decisions into a short design contract before implementation. Name the screen's job, primary action, required states, responsive rules, and patterns to reject. 4. Rebuild the useful structure in the product's own components, tokens, content, and visual language. Never copy another product's branding, proprietary text, imagery, or exact layout. Use references as evidence, not as templates. If references are unavailable, document the assumptions and verify the result against the product's existing design system. ### Avoid the AI Aesthetic AI-generated UI has recognizable patterns. Avoid all of them: | AI Default | Why It Is a Problem | Production Quality | |---|---|---| | Purple/indigo everything | Models default to visually "safe" palettes, making every app look identical | Use the project's actual color palette | | Excessive gradients | Gradients add visual noise and clash with most design systems | Flat or subtle gradients matching the design system | | Rounded everything (rounded-2xl) | Maximum rounding signals "friendly" but ignores the hierarchy of corner radii in real designs | Consistent border-radius from the design system | | Generic hero sections | Template-driven layout with no connection to the actual content or user need | Content-first layouts | | Lorem ipsum-style copy | Placeholder text hides layout problems that real content reveals (length, wrapping, overflow) | Realistic placeholder content | | Oversized padding everywhere | Equal generous padding destroys visual hierarchy and wastes screen space | Consistent spacing scale | | Stock card grids | Uniform grids are a layout shortcut that ignores information priority and scanning patterns | Purpose-driven layouts | | Shadow-heavy design | Layered shadows add depth that competes with content and slows rendering on low-end devices | Subtle or no shadows unless the design system specifies | ### Spacing and Layout Use a consistent spacing scale. Don't invent values: ```css /* Use the scale: 0.25rem increments (or whatever the project uses) */ /* Good */ padding: 1rem; /* 16px */ /* Good */ gap: 0.75rem; /* 12px */ /* Bad */ padding: 13px; /* Not on any scale */ /* Bad */ margin-top: 2.3rem; /* Not on any scale */ ``` ### Typography Respect the type hierarchy: ``` h1 → Page title (one per page) h2 → Section title h3 → Subsection title body → Default text small → Secondary/helper text ``` Don't skip heading levels. Don't use heading styles for non-heading content. ### Color - Use semantic color tokens: `text-primary`, `bg-surface`, `border-default` — not raw hex values - Ensure sufficient contrast (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text) - Don't rely solely on color to convey information (use icons, text, or patterns too) ## Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA) Every component must meet these standards: ### Keyboard Navigation ```tsx // Every interactive element must be keyboard accessible // ✓ Focusable by default
    Click me
    // ✗ Not focusable
    onKeyDown={e => { if (e.key === 'Enter') handleClick(); if (e.key === ' ') e.preventDefault(); }} onKeyUp={e => { if (e.key === ' ') handleClick(); }}> Click me
    ``` ### ARIA Labels ```tsx // Label interactive elements that lack visible text // Label form inputs // Or use aria-label when no visible label exists ``` ### Focus Management ```tsx // Move focus when content changes function Dialog({ isOpen, onClose }: DialogProps) { const closeRef = useRef(null); useEffect(() => { if (isOpen) closeRef.current?.focus(); }, [isOpen]); // Trap focus inside dialog when open return ( {/* dialog content */} ); } ``` ### Meaningful Empty and Error States ```tsx // Don't show blank screens function TaskList({ tasks }: { tasks: Task[] }) { if (tasks.length === 0) { return (

    No tasks

    Get started by creating a new task.

    ); } return
      ...
    ; } ``` ## Responsive Design Design for mobile first, then expand: ```tsx // Tailwind: mobile-first responsive
    ``` Test at these breakpoints: 320px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px. ## Loading and Transitions ```tsx // Skeleton loading (not spinners for content) function TaskListSkeleton() { return (
    {Array.from({ length: 3 }).map((_, i) => (
    ))}
    ); } // Optimistic updates for perceived speed function useToggleTask() { const queryClient = useQueryClient(); return useMutation({ mutationFn: toggleTask, onMutate: async (taskId) => { await queryClient.cancelQueries({ queryKey: ['tasks'] }); const previous = queryClient.getQueryData(['tasks']); queryClient.setQueryData(['tasks'], (old: Task[]) => old.map(t => t.id === taskId ? { ...t, done: !t.done } : t) ); return { previous }; }, onError: (_err, _taskId, context) => { queryClient.setQueryData(['tasks'], context?.previous); }, }); } ``` ## See Also For detailed accessibility requirements and testing tools, see `../../references/accessibility-checklist.md`. ## Common Rationalizations | Rationalization | Reality | |---|---| | "Accessibility is a nice-to-have" | It's a legal requirement in many jurisdictions and an engineering quality standard. | | "We'll make it responsive later" | Retrofitting responsive design is 3x harder than building it from the start. | | "The design isn't final, so I'll skip styling" | Use the design system defaults. Unstyled UI creates a broken first impression for reviewers. | | "This is just a prototype" | Prototypes become production code. Build the foundation right. | | "The AI aesthetic is fine for now" | It signals low quality. Use the project's actual design system from the start. | ## Red Flags - Components with more than 200 lines (split them) - Inline styles or arbitrary pixel values - Missing error states, loading states, or empty states - No keyboard navigation testing - Color as the sole indicator of state (red/green without text or icons) - Generic "AI look" (purple gradients, oversized cards, stock layouts) ## Verification After building UI: - [ ] Component renders without console errors - [ ] All interactive elements are keyboard accessible (Tab through the page) - [ ] Screen reader can convey the page's content and structure - [ ] Responsive: works at 320px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px - [ ] Loading, empty, error, success, and permission states handled when applicable - [ ] Follows the project's design system (spacing, colors, typography) - [ ] The rendered result passes a final UI-specific finish-gate review - [ ] No accessibility warnings in dev tools or axe-core Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\Administrator\.agents\skills\frontend-ui-engineering Relative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory. Note: file list is sampled.

The logo script is still running (pwsh 21264/21268 started at 7:30). Also, there's a new file `fDa3R-removebg-preview.png` (93KB) that the user added at 5:53 — the user probably generated a version of the logo with the background removed! This might make the entire pipeline unnecessary. Let's take a look at this file.

First, let's read the main files to fix the 3 issues. I'll read window-manager.ts, Bubble.tsx, Chat.tsx, Chat.css, Settings.tsx, and the relevant parts of ipc-handlers.ts and preload.

Let me note an interesting point: there's a `fDa3R-removebg-preview.png` in `build` (the background-removed version of your logo, which we might use later). I'll read the relevant files:

Now I understand the bubble window setup. The bubble window is 380x520 and transparent, with the bubble itself being only 60x60 in the bottom-right. The problem: the whole 380x520 window is capturing clicks around the bubble, even though it's transparent.

The fix: use `-webkit-app-region` or set the window's hit-test to only the bubble region. In Electron, a transparent window still captures input across its whole bounds. The proper fix is to make the window itself only as large as the bubble (e.g., 80x80), so clicks outside pass through to the desktop.

Let me look at the other files: main/index.ts, Chat.tsx, Settings.tsx, ipc-handlers.ts, model-client.ts, preload/index.ts, db.ts.
Ahora leo el resto de los archivos clave:
Alright, let's read App.tsx and Chat.tsx to understand the flow of the view state, and also read ipc-handlers.ts to check the connection handling and settings.
Now let's read ipc-handlers.ts and Settings.tsx to understand how settings are saved and why they don't take effect.

Ahora entiendo los tres problemas:

1. **Burbuja con hitbox transparente**: La ventana `BrowserWindow` tiene 380x520 y es `transparent: true`. Cuando la burbuja está minimizada (o el chat está cerrado), la ventana sigue teniendo el tamaño completo de 380x520, y aunque el contenido transparente no se ve, la ventana intercepta clics en toda esa área. Además, el `Bubble` se renderiza en `App.tsx` SIEMPRE, incluso cuando `showChat` es true. Entonces la burbuja (60x60) está en la esquina inferior derecha de la ventana de 380x520, y todo el espacio restante de la ventana es transparente pero captura clics.

   Solución: usar `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, { forward: true })` cuando el chat está cerrado, y desactivarlo cuando está abierto. O mejor: hacer que el contenido HTML se ajuste al tamaño real. La forma más robusta en Electron es usar `setIgnoreMouseEvents` en el main process con `forward: true`, y en el renderer controlar con `pointer-events` en las zonas.

   Pero hay un matiz: `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, { forward: true })` ignora el mouse pero reenvía los eventos. Con `forward: true`, los eventos de mouse pasan a través de la ventana a la ventana de abajo PERO el elemento debajo del cursor en la página aún recibe eventos de mouse para elementos con `pointer-events: auto`. En realidad, `forward: true` significa que los eventos de mouse se reenvían a la ventana de abajo, y `pointer-events` en CSS decide qué elementos reciben eventos.

   La técnica estándar: `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, { forward: true })` hace que la ventana sea click-through, pero los elementos con `pointer-events: auto` siguen recibiendo eventos porque `forward` reenvía. Hmm, en realidad la técnica clásica de Electron para click-through con elementos interactivos es:

   ```js
   // main
   win.setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, { forward: true });
   
   // renderer
   document.body.style.pointerEvents = 'none';
   // y en el elemento clickeable
   el.style.pointerEvents = 'auto';
   ```

   Con `forward: true`, los eventos de mouse pasan a la ventana de abajo PERO los elementos con `pointer-events: auto` aún reciben el evento primero. Espera, no exactamente. La documentación dice: con `forward: true`, los eventos de mouse se reenvían a Chromium y el elemento bajo el cursor los recibe SI tiene `pointer-events: auto`; si no, pasan a la ventana de abajo.

   En realidad el comportamiento correcto documentado:
   - `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, { forward: true })`: la ventana ignora los eventos de mouse, pero `forward: true` hace que los eventos de movimiento de mouse se reenvíen a la página web para que el DOM pueda recibir `mouseenter/mousemove` etc. en elementos con `pointer-events: auto`.
   - La clave es CSS: los elementos con `pointer-events: none` dejan pasar el clic a través; los que tienen `pointer-events: auto` lo capturan.

   Pero en la práctica, para que funcione el click-through selectivo, se usa el patrón de `mousemove` para alternar `setIgnoreMouseEvents`. Es más complicado.

   Alternativa más simple y robusta para este caso: **redimensionar la ventana** cuando la burbuja está sola. Cuando `showChat` es false, la ventana debe ser pequeña (solo la burbuja, ~68x68). Cuando `showChat` es true, la ventana debe ser grande (380x520). Esto se controla desde el main process con `win.setBounds()` y `win.setSize()`, y el renderer solo muestra la burbuja o el chat.

   Esta es la solución más limpia porque:
   - La ventana transparente pequeña solo cubre la burbuja.
   - No hay área transparente que capture clics.
   - El `Bubble` se posiciona con `position: fixed; bottom: 20; right: 20` que en una ventana pequeña sería `right: 4px` (porque la ventana es de ~64px y la burbuja 60px). Mejor posicionar la burbuja en `left: 4px; top: 4px` para que quede centrada en la ventana pequeña.

   Pero hay un detalle: cuando el chat se abre, el contenido cambia. La ventana debe cambiar de tamaño. Y cuando se cierra, volver a tamaño burbuja.

   Voy a implementar esto en el main process con IPC:
   - `ui:set-chat-mode` (o reutilizar algo). El renderer avisa al main cuando `showChat` cambia.
   - El main cambia el tamaño/posición de la ventana.

   Necesito:
   - En `App.tsx`: un `useEffect` que llame a `window.electronAPI.setChatOpen(showChat)` cada vez que cambie.
   - En preload: exponer `setChatOpen`.
   - En ipc-handlers o window-manager: manejar el resize.

   La posición de la ventana: cuando está en modo burbuja, debería estar abajo a la derecha con la burbuja en la esquina. Cuando se abre el chat, la ventana grande debería posicionarse también abajo a la derecha.

   El `BrowserWindow` actual posiciona la ventana de 380x520 en `x = screenWidth - 380 - 24`, `y = screenHeight - 520 - 80`. Eso está bien para el chat.

   Para la burbuja, la ventana debería ser de ~64x64 (burbuja 60px + borde) y posicionada en `x = screenWidth - 64 - 24`, `y = screenHeight - 64 - 20`. Pero la burbuja está en `bottom: 20; right: 20` en el CSS. Si la ventana es de 64x64 y la burbuja está en `bottom: 20; right: 20`, la burbuja quedaría desbordada. Necesito cambiar el CSS de la burbuja para que quede en `top: 2px; left: 2px` (o centrada) cuando está en modo burbuja.

   Mejor enfoque: la burbuja en CSS se posiciona `bottom: 2px; right: 2px` dentro de una ventana de 64x64. Cuando el chat está abierto, la ventana es 380x520 y la burbuja no se muestra (porque el chat la tapa) o se muestra en la esquina inferior derecha del chat. Hmm, pero cuando el chat está abierto, ¿queremos la burbuja visible? Probablemente no; el chat la reemplaza. 

   Miremos el `App.tsx` actual: siempre renderiza `Bubble`, y cuando `showChat` es true también renderiza `Chat`. La burbuja queda en la esquina inferior derecha, el chat (`.app`) ocupa toda la ventana. El chat tiene fondo oscuro opaco, así que tapa la burbuja. OK.

   Entonces el plan:
   - Modo burbuja (chat cerrado): ventana 64x64, burbuja visible ocupando toda la ventana.
   - Modo chat (abierto): ventana 380x520, burbuja oculta (o detrás), chat visible.

   Para el cambio de tamaño, debo manejar:
   1. Posición: al cambiar a chat, posicionar abajo-derecha. Al volver a burbuja, posicionar abajo-derecha (esquina).
   2. El `setBounds` con animación.

   También está el atajo global `Ctrl+Alt+J` y el tray que alternan visibilidad. `toggleWindow` hace `show()/hide()`. Si la ventana está oculta y la muestro, debería mostrar el chat (o la burbuja). El toggle de visibilidad es independiente del modo chat/burbuja.

   En realidad hay dos conceptos:
   - Visibilidad de la ventana (show/hide) — controlada por tray/atajo.

Let's actually get to work: implement the fix. Let me plan out the design:

**Architecture changes:**

The window is currently fixed at 380×520, and the bubble is a 60px circle inside it, drawn at `bottom: 20, right: 20`. Problem: the transparent area is still clickable (Windows/Chromium: transparent pixels of a transparent BrowserWindow actually do transmit clicks… hmm, actually, in Electron with `transparent: true`, transparent regions of the page do let clicks through to what's beneath—no, wait. Actually, in Electron, with `transparent: true`, clicks on transparent areas of a page pass through on Windows only when…? No, wait—actually, no: Electron's transparent windows do NOT let clicks pass through transparent regions by default; hit-testing follows the painted pixels in Chromium? Let me think.

Known fact: In Electron, `transparent: true` windows do pass mouse events through fully transparent regions on macOS and Windows? Actually the documented behavior: "transparent windows" + `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, { forward: true })` is needed to control passthrough. By default, the whole window rectangle captures mouse input regardless of pixel alpha… hmm, actually in Chromium/Electron, with a transparent window, clicks on regions where the page is transparent (alpha 0) DO fall through on Windows? No—empirically, Electron's transparent windows capture clicks across the entire rectangle (the window is rectangular for hit-testing). That's why people use `setIgnoreMouseEvents` with forward. Actually wait: there was a change—on Windows, transparent regions of layered windows are click-through if using per-pixel alpha (Windows Update Layered). Electron uses DirectComposition for transparent windows now and the entire surface captures input. Empirically, many users report that even with transparent pixels the transparent portions of the window still intercept mouse events and you have to use setIgnoreMouseEvents. The user's complaint confirms this: "cuando la burbuja está minimizada, no se puede clickear al rededor de la burbuja porque queda con el tamaño de cuando está en ventana"—the whole rectangle captures clicks.

**Best fix**: dynamically resize the actual OS window:
- Bubble mode: window is small, e.g., 110×110 (bubble 60px + shadow margin), positioned bottom-right, skipTaskbar, alwaysOnTop.
- Chat mode: expand the window to chat size (with animation is optional; just setSize + setPosition is enough), keeping the bubble in bottom-right.

Implementation: IPC `ui:set-mode` from renderer with {mode, size} → main resizes/repositions window. Or more simply: expose `setWindowSize(w,h)` and `setWindowMode('bubble'|'chat')` from preload, and let main handle positioning (anchored bottom-right of work area).

Also bubble mode needs draggable—the bubble window should ideally be draggable. With frameless windows, `-webkit-app-region: drag` works on the bubble div, with the bubble itself having `no-drag` for clicks… but a drag region can't receive clicks. Alternative: make the bubble circle a no-drag button and add a drag strip? For a 60px floating bubble, users often want to move it. Can we add: window dragging via CSS `-webkit-app-region: drag` on the bubble container and `no-drag` on the interactive circle? Then you can't drag by the circle itself. Better approach: long-press-drag via mouse events + main-process `win.setPosition` tracking with manual drag—too complex. Keep it simple: don't make the small window draggable initially? Currently it can't be moved anyway (fixed position computed at creation). The user isn't asking for dragging. Skip dragging—scope to the 3 requests. Actually, resizing the window anchored bottom-right: bubble mode anchored bottom-right, and when chat opens, the window keeps its bottom-right corner fixed while expanding left/up. This gives a natural "grow from the bubble" feel.

**Main-process helpers** (new file or inside window-manager):

const BUBBLE_SIZE = 96; // ventana solo para la burbuja
const CHAT_SIZES = { normal: {w:380,h:520}, wide: {w:560,h:680}, full: {w:900,h:640} } // tamaños
```
Persist chat size preference in settings (`chat_size`).

Function `applyWindowMode(win, mode, size)`:
- bubble: size 96×96; position: bottom-right of workArea minus margin (e.g., 16px). Bubble CSS is currently `position:fixed; bottom:20; right:20; width:60`. In a 96×96 window, position the bubble in the center of the window: change the Bubble CSS to fill the window (inset with margin 18?). More simply: window 96×96, bubble div centered (position fixed inset 0, display flex center, circle 60px).
- chat: size per settings; position: keep the bubble anchored bottom-right—that is, place the window so its bottom-right corner equals bubble-anchor + margin: x = workArea.right - margin - w, y = workArea.bottom - margin - h. Clamp to workArea.

Transition on open: setSize then show. On close (minimize to bubble): shrink back to bubble mode.

- `showChat` state drives effect: when toggled, call `window.electronAPI.setUiMode(...)`.

export function applyWindowMode(win, mode) {
  if (!win || win.isDestroyed()) return;
  currentMode = mode;
  const size = WINDOW_SIZES[mode];
  const b = win.getBounds();
  const { workArea } = screen.getDisplayMatching(b);
  const width = Math.min(size.width, workArea.width);
  const height = Math.min(size.height, workArea.height);
  const right = b.x + b.width;
  const bottom = b.y + b.height;
  let x = right - width;
  let y = bottom - height;
  x = Math.max(workArea.x, Math.min(x, workArea.x + workArea.width - width));
  y = Math.max(workArea.y, Math.min(y, workArea.y + workArea.height - height));
  win.setBounds({ x, y, width, height }, true);
}
```

Mejor enfoque: **ejecutar el build desde el anidado pero con el src de la raíz**. El anidado ya tiene su propio `src` (una copia). La forma más limpia de compilar los cambios de la RAÍZ es copiar los archivos `src` modificados al anidado, buildear ahí, y luego copiar el `dist` resultante de vuelta a la raíz. Alternativa más limpia: dado que el anidado es esencialmente una copia de trabajo del mismo proyecto, **sincronizo el `src` de la raíz → anidado**, buildeo en el anidado (que tiene node_modules funcional), y copio el `dist` a la raíz.
